about.title: Ross Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Ross is a small town, but its mix of residential properties, landscaping crews, delivery routes, and small commercial spots near Ross Common and Loma Linda Avenue means workplace injuries still happen here. Most of the time, a work injury in California goes through the workers' compensation system rather than a lawsuit against your employer. But that's not always the end of the story. If your injury involved a subcontractor, a defective piece of equipment, a negligent driver on Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, or a property owner who wasn't your direct employer, you may have a separate claim worth exploring. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free connection service. whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Ross Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: California treats workers' compensation as the usual exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be liable. An attorney can help sort out whether a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting guidance early can help protect your rights.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections before you decide what to do next.

items.question: I was hurt while working near Ross Common. Can I still file a claim outside workers' comp?
items.answer: It depends on who was responsible. If someone other than your employer, such as a delivery contractor or equipment supplier, contributed to your injury, you may be able to pursue a separate third-party claim alongside workers' comp. An attorney can look at the specifics of what happened near Ross Common and tell you whether that applies.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury under California law. If a third-party claim is involved, that typically carries its own two-year deadline. Because these timelines run separately, it helps to get clarity on both as soon as possible.

items.question: What if my employer discourages me from reporting my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California, regardless of how small your employer's operation is in a town like Ross. If you feel pressured or worried about consequences, an independent attorney can explain your rights and options before you make any decisions.
